name: b_bridge_purification
description: World bridges recomputed without the catalog entries a decision model rejects as standalone brands; the published betweenness ranking, the post-filtered ranking and the purified ranking over the same window, with a denylist control and a second window.

entity_kind.instructions: In a peer-to-peer marketplace (Mercari), sellers select a `brand_name` from a dropdown. Some entries are real standalone brands, while others are generic catch-all tags, product categories, multi-brand department stores/retailers, or mass-retailer private labels. Classify this `brand_name` entry.

criteria.standalone_brand: A genuine standalone consumer brand, fashion label, cosmetics brand, electronics/toy manufacturer, or entertainment IP (e.g., H&M, ZARA, Anthropologie, Nike, Free People, Urban Outfitters, Morphe, Tarte, Disney)
criteria.multi_brand_retailer: A department store, big-box superstore, specialty retail chain, or mall store that sells many third-party or licensed franchises under one roof (e.g., Walmart, Macy's, JCPenney, Target, Sephora, Claire's, Hot Topic, BoxLunch, Spencer's, Kohl's, Nordstrom, Costco)
criteria.superstore_house_brand: A private-label / house brand owned by a mass big-box superstore (Walmart, Target, Costco, Amazon) spanning home/apparel/general merchandise (e.g., Mainstays, Better Homes & Gardens, THRESHOLD, Time and Tru, No Boundaries, Wild Fable, Universal Thread, Cat & Jack, Room Essentials, Kirkland Signature)
criteria.generic_catchall_or_category: Not a brand at all, but a generic seller descriptor, vintage tag, infomercial label, or product type mistakenly listed as a brand (e.g., Customized & Personalized, US Vintage, American Vintage, As Seen on TV, Eyeshadow, Handmade, Boutique)

is_standalone_brand.instructions: Is this entry a genuine standalone consumer brand rather than a generic descriptor, category name, department store, or big-box private label?

criteria.true: Distinct standalone brand or creator label with its own brand identity
criteria.false: Generic catch-all tag, product category, department store/superstore, or big-box house label

wormhole_pollution.instructions: How severely does this entry act as an artificial cross-community 'wormhole' that conflates unrelated shopping communities in a brand co-liking graph?
criteria: 0 - Cohesive standalone brand representing a real, specific brand affinity
1 - Broad lifestyle/fashion retailer or specialty store with moderately diverse categories
2 - Mass-market superstore house label or department store spanning unrelated household and apparel verticals
3 - Severe graph pollutant: generic non-brand catch-all tag (e.g. 'Customized & Personalized', 'As Seen on TV', 'US Vintage', 'Eyeshadow') or universal big-box superstore ('Walmart')

sql.probe:
WITH fans AS (
  SELECT -(e.user_id + 1) AS src, CAST(i.brand_id AS BIGINT) AS dst
  FROM merrec_events e JOIN merrec_items i ON i.item_id = e.item_id
  WHERE e.event_type = 'item_like' AND i.brand_id <> 0
    AND e.event_time >= TIMESTAMP '2023-05-01' AND e.event_time < TIMESTAMP '2023-11-01'
  GROUP BY e.user_id, i.brand_id
), top_brands AS (
  SELECT dst AS brand_id, COUNT(*) AS fans FROM fans GROUP BY dst ORDER BY fans DESC, dst LIMIT 5000
), similar AS (
  SELECT first, second, similarity
  FROM cugraph_jaccard(
    edges => (SELECT src, dst FROM fans),
    vertex_pairs => (SELECT a.brand_id AS first, b.brand_id AS second
                     FROM top_brands a JOIN top_brands b ON a.brand_id < b.brand_id),
    directed => false)
  WHERE similarity >= 0.02
), worlds AS (
  SELECT vertex AS brand_id, community AS world
  FROM cugraph_leiden(
    edges => (SELECT first AS src, second AS dst, CAST(similarity AS DOUBLE) AS weight FROM similar),
    directed => false, resolution => 3, seed => 42)
), bridges AS (
  SELECT vertex AS brand_id, value AS betweenness
  FROM cugraph_betweenness_centrality(
    edges => (SELECT first AS src, second AS dst FROM similar),
    directed => false, normalized => true)
), neighbors AS (
  SELECT first AS brand_id, second AS neighbor FROM similar
  UNION ALL SELECT second, first FROM similar
), reach AS (
  SELECT n.brand_id, COUNT(*) AS neighbors, COUNT(DISTINCT w.world) AS worlds_reached
  FROM neighbors n JOIN worlds w ON w.brand_id = n.neighbor
  GROUP BY n.brand_id
), brands AS (
  SELECT CAST(brand_id AS BIGINT) AS brand_id, MIN(brand_name) AS brand_name
  FROM merrec_items WHERE brand_id <> 0 GROUP BY brand_id
)
SELECT br.brand_id, b.brand_name, t.fans, w.world, r.neighbors, r.worlds_reached, br.betweenness
FROM bridges br
JOIN worlds w ON w.brand_id = br.brand_id
JOIN reach r ON r.brand_id = br.brand_id
JOIN top_brands t ON t.brand_id = br.brand_id
JOIN brands b ON b.brand_id = br.brand_id
ORDER BY br.betweenness DESC, b.brand_name
LIMIT 120
sql.context:
WITH target_items AS (
  SELECT CAST(brand_id AS BIGINT) AS brand_id, c0_name, c1_name, category_path, name, price
  FROM merrec_items
  WHERE brand_id IN ({brand_ids})
), brand_stats AS (
  SELECT brand_id,
         COUNT(*) AS total_listings,
         COUNT(DISTINCT c0_name) AS distinct_c0,
         COUNT(DISTINCT c1_name) AS distinct_c1,
         ROUND(AVG(price), 2) AS avg_price
  FROM target_items
  GROUP BY brand_id
), top_cats AS (
  SELECT brand_id, category_path, COUNT(*) AS listings,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY brand_id ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, category_path) AS rk
  FROM target_items
  WHERE category_path IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY brand_id, category_path
), sample_titles AS (
  SELECT brand_id, name,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY brand_id ORDER BY name) AS trk
  FROM target_items
  WHERE name IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT bs.brand_id, bs.total_listings, bs.distinct_c0, bs.distinct_c1, bs.avg_price,
       MAX(CASE WHEN tc.rk = 1 THEN tc.category_path END) AS cat1,
       MAX(CASE WHEN tc.rk = 1 THEN tc.listings END) AS cat1_listings,
       MAX(CASE WHEN tc.rk = 2 THEN tc.category_path END) AS cat2,
       MAX(CASE WHEN tc.rk = 2 THEN tc.listings END) AS cat2_listings,
       MAX(CASE WHEN tc.rk = 3 THEN tc.category_path END) AS cat3,
       MAX(CASE WHEN tc.rk = 3 THEN tc.listings END) AS cat3_listings,
       MAX(CASE WHEN st.trk = 10 THEN st.name END) AS title1,
       MAX(CASE WHEN st.trk = 50 THEN st.name END) AS title2,
       MAX(CASE WHEN st.trk = 100 THEN st.name END) AS title3,
       MAX(CASE WHEN st.trk = 200 THEN st.name END) AS title4
FROM brand_stats bs
LEFT JOIN top_cats tc ON tc.brand_id = bs.brand_id AND tc.rk <= 3
LEFT JOIN sample_titles st ON st.brand_id = bs.brand_id AND st.trk IN (10, 50, 100, 200)
GROUP BY bs.brand_id, bs.total_listings, bs.distinct_c0, bs.distinct_c1, bs.avg_price
ORDER BY bs.brand_id

sql.recompute_canonical:
WITH fans AS (
  SELECT -(e.user_id + 1) AS src, COALESCE(c.canonical_id, CAST(i.brand_id AS BIGINT)) AS dst
  FROM merrec_events e JOIN merrec_items i ON i.item_id = e.item_id
  LEFT JOIN brand_ontology o ON o.brand_id = CAST(i.brand_id AS BIGINT)
  LEFT JOIN brand_canonical c ON c.brand_id = CAST(i.brand_id AS BIGINT)
  WHERE e.event_type = 'item_like' AND i.brand_id <> 0
    AND (o.brand_id IS NULL OR o.band = 'accept')
    AND e.event_time >= TIMESTAMP '2023-05-01' AND e.event_time < TIMESTAMP '2023-11-01'
  GROUP BY 1, 2
), top_brands AS (
  SELECT dst AS brand_id, COUNT(*) AS fans FROM fans GROUP BY dst ORDER BY fans DESC, dst LIMIT 5000
), similar AS (
  SELECT first, second, similarity
  FROM cugraph_jaccard(

                     FROM top_brands a JOIN top_brands b ON a.brand_id < b.brand_id),
    directed => false)
  WHERE similarity >= 0.02

  SELECT CAST(brand_id AS BIGINT) AS brand_id, MIN(brand_name) AS brand_name
